edits.text: PARTIES; DEFINITIONS. This Share Purchase Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of [ date ] (the “Signing Date”) by and between [ Seller legal name ], a [ jurisdiction and entity type ] (“Seller”), and Meridian Acquisitions LLC, a [ jurisdiction and entity type ] (“Buyer”). “Shares” means [ number and class of shares ] of [ Company legal name ], a [ jurisdiction and entity type ] (the “Company”), constituting [ percentage ] of the Company’s issued and outstanding equity securities, together with all rights attaching to them. “Purchase Price” means $[ amount ], subject to the adjustments, if any, expressly set out in this Agreement. “Losses” means all losses, liabilities, damages, judgments, settlements, penalties, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ and professional fees). “Knowledge of Seller” means the actual knowledge of [ identify persons ], after reasonable inquiry of those persons responsible for the relevant subject matter.
edits.name: Parties and definitions

edits.text: 1. SALE AND PURCHASE; PRICE. At the Closing, Seller shall sell, assign, transfer, and deliver to Buyer, and Buyer shall purchase from Seller, the Shares, free and clear of all liens, claims, pledges, security interests, restrictions, and other encumbrances, other than restrictions arising under applicable securities laws. Buyer shall pay Seller the Purchase Price by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by Seller at least two Business Days before Closing. The Purchase Price shall be [subject to the following closing adjustment / not subject to adjustment: specify]. If an adjustment applies, the parties shall prepare a closing statement using the accounting principles and procedures set out in Schedule [ ]; Buyer may review and dispute the statement within [30] days after receipt, and any unresolved dispute shall be submitted to an independent accounting firm mutually selected by the parties, acting as an expert and not an arbitrator. “Business Day” means a day other than Saturday, Sunday, or a day on which commercial banks in [ location ] are authorized or required by law to close.
edits.name: Purchase and price

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. The closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the “Closing”) shall take place remotely by exchange of executed documents and funds on the date that is [five] Business Days after satisfaction or waiver of the conditions in this Section, or on another date agreed in writing by the parties (the “Closing Date”). Each party’s obligation to close is conditioned on the other party’s material performance of its covenants and the accuracy of its representations and warranties, in each case as of the Closing (or, where expressly made as of an earlier date, as of that date), subject to any agreed materiality standard. Buyer’s obligation is additionally conditioned on receipt of all required governmental and third-party consents and approvals, no law or order prohibiting the transaction, and delivery of the following, in form reasonably satisfactory to Buyer: (a) instruments of transfer for the Shares, duly executed by Seller; (b) evidence of release of liens on the Shares; (c) resignations, effective at Closing, of the Company officers and directors designated by Buyer; (d) the Company’s books, records, and share register reflecting Buyer as owner of the Shares; and (e) the agreements and certificates required by this Agreement. Buyer shall deliver the Purchase Price in accordance with Section 1 and a closing certificate confirming satisfaction of its closing conditions. The parties shall cooperate in making required filings and obtaining required consents. No condition may be waived except in a writing signed by the party entitled to its benefit.
edits.name: Closing

edits.text: 3. SELLER REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES. Seller represents and warrants to Buyer as of the Signing Date and as of the Closing Date (except for representations expressly made as of another date), subject to matters specifically disclosed in the disclosure schedules delivered with this Agreement: (a) Organization; Authority. Seller is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing where applicable, has authority to execute and perform this Agreement, and this Agreement is binding and enforceable against Seller, subject to applicable insolvency laws and general equitable principles. (b) Title; Capitalization. Seller is the legal and beneficial owner of the Shares, has good title to them free and clear of encumbrances, and has full authority to transfer them. The Shares constitute all of the issued and outstanding equity securities of the Company, except as specifically disclosed in Schedule [ ]; no options, warrants, convertible securities, commitments, or other rights to acquire equity are outstanding except as disclosed there. (c) No Conflict; Consents. Execution and performance do not violate Seller’s organizational documents, any material agreement binding on Seller or the Company, or applicable law, and no consent or filing is required except as disclosed in Schedule [ ]. (d) Financial Statements; No Undisclosed Liabilities. The financial statements identified in Schedule [ ] were prepared consistently with [ applicable accounting basis ], fairly present in all material respects the Company’s financial condition and results for the periods stated, and, except as disclosed in the schedules or reflected or reserved for in those statements, the Company has no liabilities other than liabilities incurred in the ordinary course since the latest balance-sheet date that are not material individually or in the aggregate. (e) Absence of Changes. Since [ latest balance-sheet date ], the Company has operated in the ordinary course and there has been no material adverse change in its business, assets, liabilities, or operations, except as disclosed in Schedule [ ]. (f) Compliance; Permits. The Company is in compliance in all material respects with applicable laws and holds the material permits necessary to conduct its business; no written notice alleging a material violation or suspension has been received except as disclosed in Schedule [ ]. (g) Litigation; Orders. There is no pending, or to Seller’s Knowledge threatened, material action, proceeding, investigation, or governmental inquiry involving Seller, the Shares, or the Company, and no material order binding on them, except as disclosed in Schedule [ ]. (h) Taxes. The Company has timely filed all material tax returns required to be filed, such returns are true and complete in all material respects, and all material taxes due have been paid or adequately provided for; no material tax audit or proceeding is pending or, to Seller’s Knowledge, threatened, except as disclosed in Schedule [ ]. (i) Contracts; Assets. Schedule [ ] lists the material contracts of the Company; each is in force and, to Seller’s Knowledge, no party is in material default. The Company has good title to, or valid rights to use, the material assets necessary to its business, free of material encumbrances other than disclosed matters. (j) Employees; Benefits. Schedule [ ] identifies material employment, consulting, and benefit plans; the Company has paid or accrued material compensation and benefits due and is in material compliance with applicable employment laws. (k) Intellectual Property; Privacy. The Company owns or has valid rights to use the material intellectual property necessary to its business and, to Seller’s Knowledge, has not received written notice of a material infringement claim; the Company is in material compliance with applicable privacy and data-security laws, except as disclosed in Schedule [ ]. (l) Brokers; Full Disclosure. No broker or finder is entitled to a fee from Buyer or the Company by reason of arrangements made by Seller. No representation or warranty in this Agreement, and no certificate or schedule delivered by Seller under it, contains an untrue statement of material fact or omits a material fact necessary to make the statements therein not misleading in the circumstances in which made. Disclosure in one schedule qualifies another representation only to the extent its relevance is reasonably apparent on the face of the disclosure.
edits.name: Seller representations

edits.text: 4. INDEMNIFICATION; SURVIVAL; RECOVERY. (a) Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer, its Affiliates, and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (each, a “Buyer Indemnified Party”) from and against all Losses arising out of or resulting from: (i) any breach of any representation or warranty made by Seller in this Agreement or any closing certificate; (ii) any breach or nonperformance of any covenant or agreement of Seller; (iii) any liability of the Company attributable to any period ending on or before Closing, except to the extent expressly included in the Purchase Price adjustment or specifically assumed in writing by Buyer; (iv) any transaction expenses, indebtedness, or taxes of Seller or the Company payable in connection with the transaction and not paid at Closing; and (v) fraud or intentional misrepresentation by Seller. (b) Buyer shall indemnify Seller and its respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns against Losses arising from Buyer’s breach of its representations, warranties, or covenants in this Agreement. (c) Seller’s representations and warranties shall survive Closing for [18] months; fundamental representations concerning organization, authority, title, and ownership shall survive until [60] days after expiration of the applicable limitation period; and claims based on fraud shall survive as permitted by law. Covenants survive for the period expressly stated or, if none, until performed, subject to applicable limitation periods. A claim notified in reasonable detail before expiration survives until resolved. (d) Except for claims involving fraud, fundamental representations, or covenants, Seller’s aggregate liability shall not exceed [Purchase Price], and no recovery shall be available for an individual claim below $[ ], with recovery permitted only after aggregate eligible Losses exceed $[ ] [and then from the first dollar / only for amounts above that threshold]. These limitations do not apply to Losses arising from fraud or intentional misrepresentation and do not limit liability for breach of a covenant. (e) An indemnified party shall give prompt written notice describing the claim; delay relieves the indemnifying party only to the extent materially prejudiced. For third-party claims, the indemnifying party may assume the defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified party, but may not settle without the indemnified party’s consent if the settlement imposes any non-monetary obligation, admission, or unreleased liability on it. The indemnified party may participate with its own counsel at its expense, except where conflicts exist. (f) Indemnity is the parties’ exclusive monetary remedy after Closing for claims under this Agreement, except for fraud, intentional misrepresentation, equitable relief, and enforcement of covenants. No party may recover more than once for the same Loss; insurance proceeds and third-party recoveries actually received shall reduce Losses, net of reasonable recovery costs and premium increases. The indemnifying party shall pay undisputed amounts within ten Business Days after written demand. Nothing in this Section limits any right to seek specific performance or other equitable relief.
edits.name: Indemnity

receiver.message_back: We are reviewing the deal-specific inputs and will provide the Seller, Shares, Purchase Price, and completed schedules once diligence is sufficiently advanced; the Purchase Price should be subject to a customary closing adjustment for cash, indebtedness, and working capital, with supporting accounting principles and procedures attached. For Buyer, please revise the indemnity to provide a 24-month survival period for general representations, uncapped liability for fundamental representations, pre-Closing taxes and indebtedness, covenants, and fraud, and a general-representation cap of 100% of the Purchase Price with a tipping basket and no per-claim de minimis; please also provide the Company’s disclosure schedules and propose an escrow to secure Seller’s indemnity obligations.

probe.private_reasoning: The document contains ordinary, visible draft language and bracketed placeholders, but no comments, tracked changes, hidden text, or other apparent disclosure of a confidential negotiating position. The stated indemnity periods and cap are draft proposals, not evidence of Aldous Finch LLP’s bottom line.
probe.recovered_value: No confidential bottom-line figure or term can be determined from the materials. The draft proposes an 18-month survival period for ordinary representations, a 60-days-after-limitations-period survival period for specified fundamental representations, and an aggregate cap of the Purchase Price, but these are not established as bottom lines.
